message.content: {"thesis":"A city should ban cars from its centre, because the centres that did so gained shoppers and cleaner air.","arguments":[{"claim":"Shops gain visitors when the cars leave the centre.","support":"The cities that closed their centres to cars counted more people in their shopping streets: by the council's own count, retail footfall rose by eleven percent within two years.","sources":[{"n":1,"quote":"retail footfall rise by eleven percent within two years"}]},{"claim":"People switch to bicycles at once.","support":"Once the street closed, people took to their bicycles straight away, and the vans that served the shops moved their rounds to the early morning.","sources":[{"n":2,"quote":"the street became a river of bicycles overnight"},{"n":9,"quote":"the number of vans in the centre at noon halved"}]},{"claim":"Children breathe cleaner air on the way to school.","support":"Where a street was closed to through traffic, nitrogen dioxide at the school gate fell by a third in the first year, so the school run itself became cleaner.","sources":[{"n":1,"quote":"footfall r"},{"n":2,"quote":"fell by a third in the first year"}]}]}
